explanation: Son of Rehoboam and king over Judah, who fought against Jeroboam and his forces from Israel.
First king of the northern kingdom of Israel after the kingdom was divided into two; known for his disobedience to God and introduction of idol worship.
One of the twelve tribes of Israel and the name of the southern kingdom after the division of Israel's kingdom.
Members of the tribe of Levi, who were responsible for serving in the temple and performing priestly duties.
An agreement between God and his people, where God promises protection and blessings in exchange for obedience and faithfulness.
A structure or table where offerings and holy acts are performed as part of religious worship.
Idols shaped like calves, made of gold; Jeroboam introduced them in Israel as part of his idol worship.
The conflict between Abijah and Jeroboam, where God gave victory to Abijah and Judah.
A person who speaks on behalf of God and delivers his message to the people.
